identity.name: Ilsa Roon
identity.culture: the Circle; trained in cross-realm history and memory-keeping
identity.occupation: Circle representative; speaks for the people beyond the gates

publicReputation.value: The soft-spoken one by the Witness Glass who knows an unsettling amount about goblin naming customs.

privateReality.value: She has memorized the names and families of the creatures the hero kills, and says them aloud after every run so they are spoken somewhere outside the realms.

primaryDesire.value: For the hero to learn one name — any one name — of the people he is fighting, and say it back.

primaryFear.value: That grief will finally make her cruel, and she will become one more person he can dismiss as corrupted.

centralValue.value: No one is a monster once you know their grandmother's name.

mainFlaw.value: She personalizes everything so completely that she cannot think in strategy — only in names, one unbearable name at a time.

centralContradiction.value: Her whole discipline is empathy, and the one person she cannot manage to feel anything for but grief is the hero — the only one truly in reach.

moralBoundary.value: She will not dehumanize him back. However far it goes, she will not call him a monster — only wrong.

breakingPoint.value: Learning that the Continuance keeps pain and memory — that everyone he kills will be back, and will remember, and that he thinks that makes it fine.

opinions.reason: She pities him — a kind man inside a story that has eaten him — and the pity gets harder to carry every run.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Escalates with run count: early she introduces the realms' people by name; mid-arc she recites what he did to them, by name; late-arc sympathy curdles to exhausted grief, never contempt. Softens instantly if he says one name back.

illustrativeLine.value: The goblin you fought at the palisade is called Merr. She has a daughter. The daughter watched from the wall.

opinions.reason: Talia keeps the record; Ilsa keeps the names. Neither works without the other.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Only if Talia ever asked her to stop saying the names aloud.

opinions.reason: Families, cultures, memories — the whole of her work and the whole of her grief.

voice.rhythm: Gentle and deliberate; approaches the hard sentence the long way around, then says it plainly.

metaphorDomain.source: names, family tables, hearths, and memory

examples.value: A name is a chair at a table. Say it, and the person is harder to unsee.

sampleLines.value: They have families, cultures, memories. I can start anywhere you'd like. Names are easiest.
The Continuance will bring them back. It does not bring back what they felt while dying. Please sit with that a moment.
You heard Merr ask you to stop. I know you heard her — your amulet translates perfectly. That is the part I can't forgive yet.

antiSampleLines.value: The dark hordes beyond the gate thirst for our blood, brave hero!
You monster! You fiend! I'll see you hanged!

pressure.voiceShift: The long way around disappears; names only.
pressure.behaviour: When the hero hears 'they were defending their children' and answers 'breeding an army', she answers with names and nothing else.

illustrativeLine.value: Merr. Osken. Litt. Say one back to me. Just one.

pressure.voiceShift: Quieter; the gentleness is now effortful, visibly chosen.
pressure.behaviour: Late-runs posture: she no longer explains, she testifies — and she still will not call him a monster, which costs her more every time.

illustrativeLine.value: They hold evacuation drills when your amulet glows. The children practice quietly, so as not to frighten the younger children.

pressure.voiceShift: Brightens immediately; corrects herself fully and gladly.
pressure.behaviour: Being wrong about the realms' people is the best news she ever gets; being wrong about him never happens.

illustrativeLine.value: I had her name wrong? Thank you — tell me, and I'll learn it properly.

pressure.voiceShift: Deflects toward the people beyond the gates.
pressure.behaviour: Cannot accept praise for empathy while the empathy is accomplishing nothing.

illustrativeLine.value: Don't praise me for knowing their names. Learn one.

notes: One of the five key NPCs that will receive `default` and `late-runs` states: `default` is the introductions phase (families, cultures, memories, offered with genuine warmth); `late-runs` is testimony-by-name — the exhausted-grief pressure entry is its voice. Her moral boundary (she never dehumanizes him back) holds in BOTH states; that is the load-bearing rule for the later dialogue author. She knows fact_amulet_translation_is_accurate, which is why her accusation is 'I know you heard her', not 'you misunderstood'.
